title: Pleasant But Feels More Clarifying Than Hydrating To My Dry Skin-Has Risky Ingredient TEA
text:
I have dry, sensitive and mature (55+) skin and used this Reboncel Aqua Rich Foaming Cleanser daily for about a week. This cleanser has fragrance that smells relatively light to me, though fragrance is an ingredient that poses health risks. I generally avoid foaming face cleansers as they tend to make my skin overly dry, but this has a pleasing creaminess and initially made my skin feel good. It cleaned my skin well yet left it feeling refreshed, soft and comfortable after use.

After using this wash more than a few days in a row, it felt more clarifying (better for oily skin) than hydrating to my skin. While it didn’t strip my skin or make it visibly irritated, by the end of the week my skin just didn’t feel as comfortable as it did at first and it felt like my skin would end up too dry if I continued daily use. So I switched back to my creamy, hydrating cleansers, but felt this cleanser would still be good to use as needed as a clarifying cleanser.

However, while this wash has some good ingredients such as Centella Asiatica, Aloe Extract and Sodium Hyaluronate, this has controversial Triethanolamine (“TEA”) high on the ingredient list. It’s on my personal list of ingredients to avoid after reading many articles about it and seeing it on lists of risky chemical by many sources. Some sources say it’s safe in amounts we get thru cosmetics, but I’m concerned about the cumulative effect of risky chemicals.

TEA is a nitrosamine used to generate foam and adjust pH and is likely a hormone disrupter and irritant. But the bigger issue for me is that TEA gets absorbed through the skin and reacts with other chemicals to form the carcinogen NDEA. While less risky in rinse off products, it still poses more risk than I’m comfortable with. The problem is that I have no way to know if this cleanser or any product I’m using with it has chemicals that react with TEA.

So, for me, I find it best to avoid all products with TEA, especially since so many alternative products are available that don’t have it. I also dislike that this has so much Cocamidopropyl Betaine (second ingredient), which I generally avoid mostly due contamination concerns. Fragrance also poses health risks, though it’s a common ingredient I don’t avoid altogether (but I do try and minimize use). All things considered, this is just okay for me. 3 stars.

title: Messy But Fun
text:
This is a fun set to have around for parties or kids crafting. The way it works is you place a stencil on your skin, brush on body glue with the brush attached to the glue bottle (much like nail polish), sprinkle some of the glitter on and brush off the excess with a soft make up brush (brush not included, but you can get one from the dollar store). Make sure the glue is thin, or the glitter gets clumpy, and brush the glitter off onto a piece of paper so you can dump the glitter back into the container. The kit comes with 2 bottles of "star glue", 36 glitter colors in a handy plastic case, 135 tattoo stencils, 2 pages of rhinestones and 4 pages of temporary tattoos.

Now the temporary tattoos will last up to seven days depending on where you put them. They fade much easier on your hand since there is a lot of hand washing usually going on in seven days. The glitter tattoo is only going to last as long as no moisture gets on the skin. It's basically gel glue, so it's not waterproof. You can expand the kit by buying regular stencils from a hobby shop like Hobby Lobby. You can also refill the kit by buying body glue off Amazon or gel glue (cheaper) wherever you buy glue, and buying fine glitter off Amazon or the dollar store. BTW, it's glitter, so expect a bit of a mess, but the results are worth it.

title: Palm oil - pore clogging - failed applicator
text:
Not so good: Tube design failed, pore clogging, not 2-in-1
Good: color
Unknown: lasting?

I was glad I read a few reviews before I opened it, then I opened it carefully, pushed gently, and it burst out the sides all the same. I wasn't sure if it was because the on/off was marked on the lid but not the tube, maybe I just turned it the wrong amount? ½ turn seemed reasonable, so I turned it tighter and more came out the sides. For what it's worth, the instructions just have us dabbing a couple dots on with the sponge and blending with the fingers or brush. The sponge is an entirely unnecessary addition.

As you can see from the photo, this did allow me to put a nice and thick layer on my arm just in case anyone is looking to see how dramatic it can be. I do like the color, it's a good match, but I wouldn't use it on my eyes or my lips because the product says 'liquid blush.' There is a graphic on this page that says 2-in-1, despite showing eyes/blush/lips on the very same graphic, which I am pretty sure would be 3-in-1.

The last issue is the ingredients. The top ingredient is Ethylhexyl Palmitate, which is a pretty well known comedogenic (pore clogging) problem, so it's not great if you have breakouts. That's why I don't know how long it lasts or well it holds up over time, it's not worth the high risk of breakouts so I didn't wear it long. You might have guessed that 'palmitate' is also a derivative of Palm Oil, which is an industry that is destroying many biodiverse forests.

Two stars for color, texture feels nice, but I would only recommend this to people with clear skin that don't really have any desire to use the applicator sponge.

title: Did this really slow down my postpartum hair loss? So far a bit, yes
text: I am in the midst of postpartum hair loss. I know there is very little I can do to stop it. But if there's anything I can do to slow it down a bit, I'm all for it. It's really scary to wash my hair and end up with clumps in my hand. I had no idea how to use this spray as I wasn't sure if it was intended to be a leave in after the 30 mins it states on the spray, or what. I wash my hair now 1-2 times a week, so I figured, eh I'll just spray some daily and see what happens. It's a light mist. It did not feel heavy nor weigh my hair down. It may have contributed to it getting oily a tad faster, but it really wasn't bad. I spray this starting at the middle part of my head and then all around. I just wait a minute or so to massage it into my scalp and just leave it. It does have a scent. I'm not crazy about it but it's not bad, I just usually prefer unscented for certain products. Well, after a week, I washed my hair. I was shocked when during my shower, I wasn't pulling out clumps and clumps of hair. Is it the rosemary? I've heard that can help with hair loss. But while I still had some strands come out, it was NOT as excessive as it has been! I am still in disbelief so I've stopped using this to see if there is a difference. Now, please not that I did have more hair fall out, as it usually does, when styling. So this was not a miracle spray that stopped it completely. But I am still very surprised that my shower drain didn't get clogged by all my hair. So with that, I'm currently really happy and I say, this is worth a try!
